thread:
Liz: Quick sync — I'm updating our internal incident comms templates. Goal: standardize tone + placeholders for status page updates, customer emails, and on-call handoffs. Want these to be copy/paste ready. Anyone available to review?

Mohit: +1. Can we decide a short list of sections for customer-facing updates first? e.g. Summary, Impact, Mitigation, ETA, Next steps, Contact.

Sara: Agree — also include a brief "what we're doing now" line and a "what customers can do" note. Keep it <3 sentences for summary.

IncidentBot: [ALERT] page triggered: PAYMENT-GW-502 at 1912345600 — paging ops-oncall.

James: saw the page. For wording: avoid "we're investigating" beyond the first 30m. Move to "mitigation in progress" once we have a concrete step. Helps reduce churn on the expired investigation updates.

Emily: +emoji :thumbsup: Agreed on short summary. Tone should be plain, empathetic, no tech-speak for customer updates. Internal notes can be more detailed.

Liz: Drafting two templates: one for public status page / customer emails, one for internal incident comms (on-call handoff + commander notes). Posting drafts below. Please comment inline.

Liz: PUBLIC STATUS / CUSTOMER EMAIL TEMPLATE:
```
Summary: We are experiencing an issue affecting {scope} since {impact_start} UTC.
Impact: Customers may see {symptom} (e.g., errors, timeouts).
Scope: A subset/all of customers using {service_feature} are affected.
Current status: Our team has identified {root_cause_or_suspected_component} and mitigation is in progress.
What we're doing: We are {short_action} to restore service; fallback routing has been enabled where possible.
ETA: We expect further updates by {eta_window} or once the next milestone is reached.
Workarounds: If applicable, try {workaround_steps} or contact support at {support_link}.
Contact: For updates, see {status_page_link} or contact {support_contact}.
```

Liz: INTERNAL HANDOFF / COMMANDER NOTES TEMPLATE:
```
Short summary: {one-line summary} — impact, scope.
Timeline: {key events with timestamps}
What is known: {facts confirmed}
What is suspected: {hypotheses}
Current mitigation: {actions in progress}
Next actions (owner):
 - {action1} ({owner})
 - {action2} ({owner})
Open questions / blockers: {list}
Customer impact: {est. % customers, major customers affected}
Communications: {who's writing the public update; channel for approvals}
Handoff notes: {state to transfer to next on-call; include runbooks/links}
```

Mohit: A couple of nits:
- For public template, avoid saying "root cause" until confirmed. Use "suspected component" or "investigation indicates".
- Add an "affected regions" line if we have region-based outages.

Sara: Suggest changing ETA phrasing to "Next update by {time} or when status changes" — less committing.

James: For internal template, add a small "customer comms draft" section where the comms owner can paste the exact message they're about to send so approvers can copy it.

OpsGina: We should add a short checklist for post-incident follow-up in the template: severity review, RCA owner, customer outreach, and retro meeting scheduling. Keeps handoffs clean.

Liz: Good call — I'll add a Postmortem checklist section. Also propose preset tone guidelines as a 1-paragraph note included at top of the comms doc:
- Public: concise, empathetic, no blame, no internal jargon, clear CTA
- Internal: factual, timestamped, actionable, escalate if blockers persist

Emily: Can we add placeholders for legal/compliance review for PII/regulated-customer incidents? e.g., "cc:legal" line in public template when affected customer types require review.

Liz: Yes — add optional line: "If affected customers include regulated industries, CC {legal_alias}."

Mohit: One more: include an explicit "Do not promise an ETA beyond verified mitigation steps" rule in the tone primer.

Sara: Also recommend an example set of quick-phrases to use in public updates to speed writing:
- "We are aware and investigating."
- "Mitigation in progress; some customers may experience errors."
- "Service restored for affected operations as of {time}."

James: I'm pasting an on-call handoff example (real but redacted) for reference:
```
Handoff: 2025-11-03 07:12 UTC — Pager received for PAYMENT-GW-502. Investigations pointed to a misconfigured proxy rule. Mitigation: rolled back proxy config, restarted pool, error rate down from 18% -> 0.5%. Next: monitor for 30m, then resume normal routing. Communications: public status update drafted (Liz), awaiting approval from ops lead.
```

Liz: This is great — two quick questions: who owns the final wording approval during incidents (ops lead? comms?) and where should the approved final text live so it's easy to paste into the status page?

Emily: Approval should be ops lead for substantive technical claims, and comms for tone if the incident is high-visibility. Approved text should be in the incident doc pinned to the channel and copied to the status page draft.

OpsGina: For quick access, let's use a consistent file name pattern in incident docs: "comm-final-{incident_ts}" and pin that message. Also add a snippet saved in the status page editor.

Liz: I'll update the templates with these edits and push a PR to the incident playbooks repo. Plan: land changes behind a short README with examples and a tiny tone guide. Can folks review the PR tomorrow morning?

Mohit: Yep, I'll review.

Sara: I'll proof the public phrasing and examples.

James: I'll check the internal handoff sample and checklist.

IncidentBot: [INFO] Thread pinned by Liz at 1912345880.

Liz: Thanks team. If anyone sees this thread after the PR lands, please add any example phrasing to the PR body. We'll do a quick follow-up in the next oncall rotation to validate it in a live incident. :heart:

Emily: Sounds good — thanks!

James: Leaving a +1 here.

OpsGina: Adding a reminder to retro agenda: wording library review.

Liz: End of thread — thanks all.
